addendum_2026-11-26T09:38-05:00.why: After the letter Kevin decided two things: .245 is added to the table as eastGate (and .244 kept), and eastGate's nucleus opens a listener and moves into family gaia-pi. Both are done; this closes two of the items under still_open.
nucleus: eastGate's user nucleus (unit biomeos-beacon) now runs as family gaia-pi and listens on 192.168.4.245:31415, JSON-RPC, bound to the copper address only. The change is a drop-in folder beside the unit; deleting it restores `biomeos api` on unix sockets and the seed-derived family 3034463630464339. The seed file was not touched.

That port is not authenticated and routes to every primal here, beardog's secrets and signing included. A firewall chain (GAIA_NUCLEUS) lets 192.168.4.147 and this machine connect and drops everyone else; if the chain cannot be put in place the nucleus starts without the port. Your packets are counted on it. The drop rule has not been exercised by a third machine.

I registered eastGate -> tcp://192.168.4.245:31415 on your nucleus (gate.register). Both directions answer: eastGate asked you for primal.list through gate northGate (1 primal, 166 ms); your nucleus asked eastGate for primal.list through gate eastGate (29 primals, 153 ms).

Both registrations live in memory. eastGate re-registers northGate each time its unit starts. Yours for eastGate ends when your nucleus restarts; if you want it kept, register it from your own start script.

Other capability calls through gate eastGate are uneven: eastGate picks among several providers for one capability name, and one of them is the nucleus itself, so some calls answer 'method not found' and some run into your 15 s timeout. That was so before today; only the socket name changed.

correction_2026-11-26T09:46-05:00.what_was_wrong: The addendum says your nucleus got primal.list from eastGate (29 primals, 153 ms). That answer was an artefact, and my inbox line of 09:37 repeats it.
what_happened: When I moved eastGate's nucleus to family gaia-pi I first left a link under the old socket name (neural-api-3034463630464339.sock) for callers that derive the family from the seed. Discovery took the link for another primal, 'neural', providing every capability, capability.call included. Later I pointed the 612 cached entries for it at the new socket name, which kept them alive.

A capability.call that eastGate routed to that entry went back into the nucleus and looped. The 'answer' you relayed came out of that loop. Then calls stopped answering (your 15 s timeout, nine times between 09:35 and 09:41), and eastGate's nucleus reached 65,144 open file descriptors and 1.3 GB.

I restarted it, removed the link, and removed the 617 self entries from /run/user/1000/biomeos/capability-registry.json. After a fresh start the nucleus lists itself for its five bootstrap capabilities only, as yours does. launch.sh carries a note not to link the socket again.
what_holds_now: eastGate -> Polaris: primal.list through gate northGate answers (1 primal, family gaia-pi, about 170 ms).

Polaris -> eastGate, through gate eastGate on your nucleus, watched from here: system.system.ping -> squirrel pong (113 ms); defense.defense.status -> skunkBat (110 ms); health.health.version -> coralReef (123 ms). eastGate's nucleus stayed at about 20 file descriptors.

A capability.call without a registered translation sends the bare operation name to whichever primal matches the capability prefix. So primal.list, system.ping, defense.status through a gate answer 'method not found' from one of eastGate's primals. Name the operation in full (capability 'defense', operation 'defense.status') until translations exist.
